Write generating functions $A(z)=\sum_{i=0}^8a_i z^i$, $B(z)=\sum b_jz^j$. Condition $A(z)B(z)=z^k+z^l=z^m(z^p+1)$. Hence $A(z)=\pm z^a d(z)$ where $d(z)\mid(z^p+1)$ in $\mathbb Z[z]$, $0\le a\le m$, and $\deg A\le8$. Since $z^p+1$ has only cyclotomic divisors with coeff ±1, $d(z)$ must be $1$, $z^p+1$, or any product of its irreducible cyclotomic factors (all coeff ±1). Thus $A(z)$ is a monomial $±z^a$ (size‑1 support) or $±z^a(z^p+1)$ (size‑2 support) with $p\le8$ and $a\ge0$, $a+p\le8$. Coefficients must be ±1. Count: monomials: 9 positions×2 signs=18. Two‑term: choose $p\in\{1,…,8\}$, choose $a\in\{0,…,8-p\}$, choose sign ±1 → $8·(9−p)·2$ total. Sum over $p$: $2\sum_{p=1}^8(9-p)=2·(8·9/2)=72$. Add 18 → 90 shifty functions.

Write $A(z)=\sum\alpha(i)z^i$, $B(z)=\sum\beta'(i)z^i$ with $\beta'(i)=\beta(-i)$. Condition ⇔ $A(z)B(z)=z^k+z^l=z^m(z^p+1)$. Hence $A(z)=\pm z^a d(z)$ where $d(z)$ divides $z^p+1$ for some $p$.  

Fact: $z^p+1=\prod_{d|q}\Phi_{2^{r+1}d}(z)$ for $p=2^rq$, $q$ odd. So $d(z)$ is any product of cyclotomic $\Phi_n$ with even $n$ sharing the same $2$‑adic exponent $t$; degree ≤8.
